ticket.title: Fix (review): music_video mid-turn mount (web-studio server + idea_writer agent) — 5 findings

detail.content: Now start the investigation in a coding session.

Verdict: **CHANGES NEEDED.** I filed one fix ticket, TEAM-5269, for the bug fixer, and parked my review ticket TEAM-5262 as blocked on it.

The fix does address the root cause. The agent's campaign id

was set before the music video journey was mounted, so every music video tool refused. The agent then fell back to the general-purpose card tools, and the music video canvas silently dropped their cards. The M

P3 dropped into chat was never recorded as the campaign's song. The fix works in the normal case, but it has five problems. I reviewed the merge of PR #635 into the shared fix branch (`ef473bf`), which is up

to date with main.

**Findings, all in TEAM-5269:**
1. **P1 – a session can end up writing into another user's campaign.**
   - **Cause:** the reserved campaign id is `text-music_video-<seconds>` (`server.py:3017`

), so two sessions that start a turn in the same second get the same id. When the id is already taken, the fallback (`server.py:5970`) creates the row with no "only if it doesn't exist" check.
   - **

Same second:** the fallback mints the same id again and overwrites the existing campaign row.
   - **A second later:** the new row gets a different id, but the agent stays on the first one. If both users share a

brand (such as `general`), the brand check passes and the agent edits the other user's campaign. The code comment saying this "fails closed" is wrong.
   - **Evidence:** codex reproduced both cases against the

real functions. The new test never covers a same-second clash.
2. **P2 – the chat MP3 can overwrite a song uploaded at the same moment.** The attach step (`server.py:14853-14863`) checks for an existing song, then writes

without a condition. An upload that lands in between gets replaced by the chat MP3, including the stored file. Reproduced.
3. **P2 – the agent is told the song is ready before it is.** The agent is told

"the song is already on it" before the server has created the row or attached the song. The campaign lookup can return "unknown campaign" if it runs too early. If attaching fails, it is only logged, and the ag

ent and user are never told.
4. **P2 – only four of the general-purpose card tools are blocked.** `show_idea`, `show_arc`, `show_song` and `set_subtitles` now refuse on music video. `show_scenes`, `show_clips`, `

show_caption`, `show_voiceover` and `show_goal` still draw nothing there, and they skip the new status line. So the canvas can still stay empty if the agent picks one of those.
5. **P2 – the fix is lost if the stream

breaks and the turn resumes.** The retry resends the original empty campaign id, and only the journey-mount step adopts the reserved one. The developer had already noted this as follow-up TEAM-5268; I folded it into

TEAM-5269.

**What checked out:**
- **Tests:** the three new test files pass on the branch (21, 10 and 9/9). Run against main they fail (15 failed, 7 failed, 6 of 9 failing), so they do exercise the failure path.

They are unit tests with AWS stubbed out, not end-to-end proof.
- **Long-form video (TEAM-4783):** its canvas handling is untouched; the 11 journey-summary tests pass. The new refusals fire only on music video.
-

**Shared upload handling:** explicitly uploading a new song still replaces the old one, so the shared upload path is not regressed.
- **Security and data:** the reserved id is generated by the server and p

attern-checked, not set by the client. No new database fields are stored.

**Not covered:** nothing was run live against deployed Juno or real DynamoDB, so the findings rest on reading the code plus codex prob

es with stubbed AWS. I also couldn't test whether the model actually switches to the music video tools after a refusal. The session logs and the bug screenshot were unavailable.

The full write-up is at `workflows
/wf_bug_TEAM-5259/shared/findings.md`. For the re-review I'll resume codex session `cc-cf68e9fbf0044cc68fe058191881862e`.
Now sync the integration branch with main.

ticket.title: Fix (review): music_video mid-turn mount readiness/retry (idea_writer mv_tools + web-studio server) — 4 findings
Follow-up: web-review backend timestamp campaign ids + unconditional put_item (collision overwrite)

detail.content:
**Round 2 verdict: CHANGES NEEDED.** Four of the five round-1 findings are fixed, but the third is only partly fixed. I filed TEAM-5271 for the bug fixer and parked my review ticket TEAM-5262 as blocked on it.

I re

viewed the shared fix branch after PR #636 was merged into it (`7621e2d`). The branch is not behind main. Codex checked each round-1 finding against the real functions with AWS stubbed out, not against

live Juno or real DynamoDB/S3.

**Fixed:**
- **F1 (the P1, one session writing into another user's campaign):** campaigns are now created with "only if it doesn't exist" and a retry, and two sessions

starting in the same second get different ids. If an id is already taken, the agent refuses the other row instead of writing to it, even when both users share a brand. That interrupts the turn but writes nothing wrong

.
- **F2 (chat MP3 overwriting an upload):** the chat MP3 goes to its own file, and the write only succeeds if no upload has landed. A song uploaded at the same moment is kept, even when both are MP3s.
- **F4

(cards dropped by general-purpose tools):** the block is now built from the agent's full tool list, so it covers all 48 tools that would paint nothing, not 4.
- **F5 (binding lost on stream retry):** the resumed request

now carries the mounted campaign and journey.

**Still open, all P2, all in TEAM-5271:**
- **R2-1 – the readiness check only protects the first lookup.** After the agent's first lookup of the new campaign, later tool

calls go back to a read that can be stale. That read can return "unknown campaign" again, or the row as it was before the song was attached (`mv_tools.py:154/260`).
- **R2-2 – a failed song attach is for

gotten after a resume.** The check for a saved attach error only runs on the first binding (`mv_tools.py:273`). On a stream resume or any later turn, the campaign with no song is accepted with no error

.
- **R2-3 – the promised retry is lost when the session is saved and reloaded.** The "retry the attach on the next message" flag is not saved with the session (`server.py:14980/3033/1458`). After a server restart or cold

reload the retry never runs.
- **R2-4 – one more copy of the round-1 collision pattern.** `burn_captions` (`cloud_tools.py:3164`) creates a scratch campaign from a timestamp id with no "only if it doesn

't exist" check. This was visible in round 1 and I missed it then, so it's marked as a late finding.

The same collision pattern also exists in five places in the web-review backend, which is a separate deploy

able and wasn't touched by this diff. I filed those as TEAM-5272 for the backend dev, labelled advisory. My review isn't waiting on it, so this run can ship with those five sites still unfixed.

**Tests:** 449

Python and 16 Node tests pass on the fix branch, including the long_form_video, thumbnail and routing suites. On the previous head (`ef473bf`) the new tests fail (16, 61 and 6 failures), so they do catch the round

-1 bugs. They don't cover the four open scenarios above.

Findings are in `workflows/wf_bug_TEAM-5259/shared/findings.md`. When TEAM-5271 closes I'll re-review just the new changes in the same codex session (
`cc-cf68e9fbf0044cc68fe058191881862e`). If that round still needs changes, it goes to a human instead of a third fix ticket.

**The open problem (R3-1, P2):

ug is about.

, not a live run.
- **Same problem elsewhere:** six other campaign checks in the same file use the same kind of read: lines 14539–14541, 6939, 13769, 14463, 15801 and 16567. TEAM-5274 asks for one shared helper that does

a consistent read and covers all seven. It also asks for a regression test that fails on `7ce04c6`.

The findings are updated in `workflows/wf_bug_TEAM-5259/shared/findings.md` (round 4 added). When TEA

M-5274 closes, the review restarts automatically.
